subject: Artifact residency and visibility: clarifying default behavior for request/response data
messages:
From: Lydia Chen <lydia@acme-inc.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on where request/response artifacts live by default

Hi Aditya,

Quick question from our security team: when we send requests to the hosted API, what is stored by default and where does it reside? Specifically we need to know whether:

- Full request/response payloads (prompts + model outputs) are persisted by Redwood by default
- If persisted, whether they reside in US-only storage or are replicated across regions
- How we can opt out or request deletion for customer-specific artifacts

We are doing a light MRAP exercise and need the default behavior for your hosted offering to document in our controls.

Thanks,
Lydia
Security Engineer, Acme

---
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Lydia Chen <lydia@acme-inc.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on where request/response artifacts live by default

Hi Lydia — thanks for the question and sorry for the delay. Short answer up front: by default we retain request and response artifacts for hosted API customers for troubleshooting and quality monitoring, but there are clear controls and residency options available. See a brief summary below; I attached our one-page retention summary.

What we store by default (hosted API):
- Request metadata: timestamps, model id, sequence lengths, routing decisions — retained for analytics and billing.
- Request payload (prompts): stored by default to support quality monitoring and prompt-derived evals.
- Model outputs (responses): stored by default but treated as paired artifacts with prompts; used for debugging and alerting.

Residency: default hosted storage is regionally partitioned — data from US customers is stored in US regions by default. We do not replicate hosted customer artifacts cross-region unless a customer enables multi-region replication.

Controls you can use:
- Opt-out: account setting to disable storing request/response bodies (prompts/outputs) while preserving metadata for billing.
- Deletion: per-account data purge API (or ask your AM) that removes persisted artifacts subject to retention windows.
- Private deployments (VPC/on-prem): provide full control over residency and retention (no Redwood-hosted storage).

I'll loop in Marissa (security/compliance) to confirm nuances for MRAP and SOC2 references.

Attachment: redwood-retention-one-pager.pdf (summary)

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Lydia Chen <lydia@acme-inc.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 14:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on where request/response artifacts live by default

Hi Lydia — adding a couple specifics from the compliance side to make sure your MRAP notes are accurate.

1) Retention windows and default TTLs:
- Metadata (billing/analytics): 13 months by default, can be extended for enterprise contracts.
- Full request/response bodies (prompts + outputs): default retention is 90 days for hosted accounts. This is to balance debugging/evals with user privacy.

2) Deletion semantics:
- Ad hoc deletion requests: we expose a customer data purge API that marks artifacts for deletion and schedules a background purge; typical completion time is 48–72 hours depending on backlog.
- Persistent backups / cold storage: we do not retain request/response bodies in longer-term backup systems beyond the default TTL; backups contain only metadata indexes.

3) Residency and cross‑region copies:
- Default: US-hosted accounts -> stored in US regional storage (single-region), not automatically replicated.
- If you require EU-only residency we offer a regional tenant; data will be confined to EU regions and logs will be segregated.

4) Audit evidence and SOC2:
- We can share SOC2 Type II excerpts that speak to data access controls and deletion processes. See attached excerpt; full reports are available under NDA.

5) What counts as a stored artifact:
- Stored: full prompt text, system messages, model output tokens, and generated embeddings if enabled.
- Not stored by default: ephemeral in-memory traces used solely for routing/latency (these are not persisted).

If you want, we can run a short MRAP-friendly export that lists the default retention values for each artifact class for your documentation.

—Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2-Type2-excerpt.pdf (excerpt for controls relevant to retention & deletion)

From: Lydia Chen <lydia@acme-inc.com>

Also, one note for the MRAP doc: can you call out explicitly that "embeddings generated by API calls are treated as stored artifacts"? Please confirm so we can mark the control.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Lydia
Security Engineer, Acme
